title: Dynamical Critical Properties of the Random-Bond three-state Potts Model
authors: Zeynep Demir Vatansever, Ulvi Kanbur, Mohammed Sadra Najafi, Muktish Acharyya, Erol Vatansever
abstract: We study the dynamic critical behavior of the two-dimensional random-bond three-state Potts model using large-scale Monte Carlo simulations with the Wolff and Swendsen--Wang cluster algorithms. At the disorder-dependent critical temperature, we compute integrated and exponential autocorrelation times and extract the dynamic critical exponent $z$ via finite-size scaling. Critical slowing down is significantly weakened by bond randomness, with the dynamic exponent decreasing from $z \approx 0.54$ in the pure system to $z \approx 0.24$ at strong disorder. From the finite-size scaling of the Wolff cluster size, we obtain $γ/ν\approx 1.73$, where $γ$ and $ν$ are the susceptibility and correlation-length exponents, respectively, consistent with the universality class of the two-dimensional three-state Potts model. These results indicate that bond randomness strongly affects the critical dynamics but leaves the underlying static universality class unchanged. Furthermore, both static and dynamic observables, including the specific heat and the autocorrelation times, show a lack of self-averaging.
summary: This work analyzes the critical dynamics of the random-bond three-state Potts model using advanced Monte Carlo simulations. The key finding is that bond randomness substantially weakens critical slowing down, changing the dynamic exponent. Crucially, this dynamic change occurs without altering the underlying static universality class of the model.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamic critical behavior and the influence of bond randomness on the critical slowing down of the two-dimensional three-state Potts model.
main_result:
Bond randomness significantly weakens critical slowing down, decreasing the dynamic exponent from $z \approx 0.54$ (pure) to $z \approx 0.24$ (strong disorder), while preserving the static universality class ($\gamma/
u \approx 1.73$).
method: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations utilizing Wolff and Swendsen-Wang cluster algorithms were employed to calculate time autocorrelation functions and perform finite-size scaling analyses.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional random-bond three-state Potts model, described by a Hamiltonian with random ferromagnetic interactions $J_{ij}$ drawn from a bimodal distribution.
key_observables:
Dynamic critical exponent ($z$), integrated and exponential autocorrelation times ($	au_{A,int}, 	au_{A,exp}$), and the ratio of static exponents ($\gamma/
u$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($r = J_2/J_1$), system size ($L$), and the critical temperature ($T_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the cluster algorithms and relies on finite-size scaling theory to extract critical exponents.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the systematic decrease of autocorrelation times with increasing disorder, the non-vanishing variance of static observables (specific heat), and the consistency of the exponent ratio $\gamma/
u$ across different disorder strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamic critical slowing down by calculating autocorrelation times for various disorder strengths, confirming the weakening of dynamics while verifying the robustness of the static critical exponents.
why_interesting: The findings on how quenched disorder modifies dynamic scaling exponents while preserving static universality provide valuable insights into the interplay between disorder and critical phenomena, relevant for understanding complex many-body systems.
